es: Reconocer la estructura de una charla (apertura, guía y cierre) y las expresiones que la organizan.

vocabulary.es: idea final, mensaje que se lleva el público

teaching.en: Here is my hook: have you ever wondered where your plastic goes?
teaching.es: Este es mi gancho: ¿te has preguntado alguna vez adónde va tu plástico?
teaching.explanationEs: Un hook abre la charla con una pregunta, una cifra o una imagen que despierta curiosidad.
segments: Here is my hook: have you
ever wondered where your plastic goes?
teaching.audioText: Here is my hook: have you ever wondered where your plastic goes?

teaching.en: Today I will outline three ideas: the problem, the causes and one solution.
teaching.es: Hoy presentaré tres ideas: el problema, las causas y una solución.
teaching.explanationEs: I will outline + lista: la apertura anuncia la estructura de la charla.
segments: Today I will outline three ideas: the
problem, the causes and one solution.
teaching.audioText: Today I will outline three ideas: the problem, the causes and one solution.

teaching.en: A clear transition helps: now let me move on to my second point, the causes.
teaching.es: Una transición clara ayuda: ahora paso a mi segundo punto, las causas.
teaching.explanationEs: Una transición dice al público dónde estamos y adónde vamos; let me move on to… es la fórmula más habitual.
segments: A clear transition helps: now let me move
on to my second point, the causes.
teaching.audioText: A clear transition helps: now let me move on to my second point, the causes.

teaching.en: To recap, we have seen three causes and one solution.
teaching.es: Para recapitular, hemos visto tres causas y una solución.
teaching.explanationEs: To recap resume lo dicho antes de cerrar.
segments: To recap, we have seen
three causes and one solution.
teaching.audioText: To recap, we have seen three causes and one solution.

teaching.en: My takeaway is simple: small habits change big results.
teaching.es: Mi idea final es sencilla: los pequeños hábitos cambian grandes resultados.
teaching.explanationEs: El takeaway es el mensaje que quieres que el público recuerde.
segments: My takeaway is simple: small
habits change big results.
teaching.audioText: My takeaway is simple: small habits change big results.

teaching.en: To conclude, I would like to thank the whole audience for listening.
teaching.es: Para concluir, me gustaría agradecer a todo el público por escuchar.
teaching.explanationEs: To conclude anuncia que llega el final; se agradece y se invita a preguntar.
segments: To conclude, I would like to
thank the whole audience for listening.
teaching.audioText: To conclude, I would like to thank the whole audience for listening.

es: Usar acento enfático, pausas y entonación para destacar lo importante al hablar.

teaching.en: I want to emphasise one word: this offer is FREE.
teaching.es: Quiero destacar una palabra: esta oferta es GRATIS.
teaching.explanationEs: Las mayúsculas marcan la palabra con acento enfático: sube el tono y suena más larga.
segments: I want to emphasise one
word: this offer is FREE.
teaching.audioText: I want to emphasise one word: this offer is FREE.

teaching.en: He stressed the word THOUSAND: we need ten thousand volunteers, not ten.
teaching.es: Acentuó la palabra THOUSAND: necesitamos diez mil voluntarios, no diez.
teaching.explanationEs: El acento enfático va en la palabra que corrige o contrasta con lo anterior.
segments: He stressed the word THOUSAND: we
need ten thousand volunteers, not ten.
teaching.audioText: He stressed the word THOUSAND: we need ten thousand volunteers, not ten.

teaching.en: Take a short pause before the key number, and the audience will listen.
teaching.es: Haz una pausa corta antes de la cifra clave y el público escuchará.
teaching.explanationEs: La pausa antes de la cifra crea expectativa; después de ella, deja tiempo al público para pensar.
segments: Take a short pause before the key
number, and the audience will listen.
teaching.audioText: Take a short pause before the key number, and the audience will listen.

teaching.en: Keep a steady pace: if you speak too fast, nobody can follow you.
teaching.es: Mantén un ritmo constante: si hablas demasiado rápido, nadie puede seguirte.
teaching.explanationEs: Pace es la velocidad al hablar; baja el ritmo en los datos clave.
segments: Keep a steady pace: if you speak
too fast, nobody can follow you.
teaching.audioText: Keep a steady pace: if you speak too fast, nobody can follow you.

teaching.en: Let your intonation fall at the end of a statement: we open at nine.
teaching.es: Deja que tu entonación baje al final de una afirmación: abrimos a las nueve.
teaching.explanationEs: Entonación descendente: la frase queda cerrada.
segments: Let your intonation fall at the end
of a statement: we open at nine.
teaching.audioText: Let your intonation fall at the end of a statement: we open at nine.

teaching.en: Does your voice rise at the end of a question like: are you ready?
teaching.es: ¿Sube tu voz al final de una pregunta como: are you ready?
teaching.explanationEs: Entonación ascendente: pregunta de sí o no.
segments: Does your voice rise at the end
of a question like: are you ready?
teaching.audioText: Does your voice rise at the end of a question like: are you ready?

es: Analizar por qué funciona una charla: reconocer cinco recursos y explicar su efecto en el público.

teaching.en: She began with an anecdote about her first day as a volunteer.
teaching.es: Empezó con una anécdota sobre su primer día como voluntaria.
teaching.explanationEs: Una anécdota es una historia breve y personal; hace que el público se identifique.
segments: She began with an anecdote about
her first day as a volunteer.
teaching.audioText: She began with an anecdote about her first day as a volunteer.

teaching.en: The vivid details made the story easy to picture.

teaching.explanationEs: Vivid = que crea una imagen clara en la mente; make + objeto + verbo base.
segments: The vivid details made the
story easy to picture.
teaching.audioText: The vivid details made the story easy to picture.

teaching.en: By repeating the phrase «not today», he made the message memorable.
teaching.es: Al repetir la frase «hoy no», hizo el mensaje memorable.
teaching.explanationEs: By + -ing explica cómo se consigue el efecto: la repetición ayuda a recordar.
segments: By repeating the phrase «not today»,
he made the message memorable.
teaching.audioText: By repeating the phrase «not today», he made the message memorable.

teaching.en: The contrast between a dirty river and a clean one helps to persuade the audience.
teaching.es: El contraste entre un río sucio y uno limpio ayuda a persuadir al público.
teaching.explanationEs: Un contraste pone dos imágenes opuestas frente a frente; helps to + verbo dice para qué sirve.
segments: The contrast between a dirty river and a
clean one helps to persuade the audience.
teaching.audioText: The contrast between a dirty river and a clean one helps to persuade the audience.

teaching.en: Her rhetorical question, «Who will act if we do not?», made everyone think.
teaching.es: Su pregunta retórica, «¿Quién actuará si no lo hacemos?», hizo pensar a todos.
teaching.explanationEs: Una pregunta retórica no espera respuesta: invita a reflexionar.
segments: Her rhetorical question, «Who will act if
we do not?», made everyone think.
teaching.audioText: Her rhetorical question, «Who will act if we do not?», made everyone think.

teaching.en: These techniques engage the audience because they create emotion and curiosity.
teaching.es: Estos recursos captan al público porque crean emoción y curiosidad.
teaching.explanationEs: Engage = captar y mantener la atención; se explica con because + efecto.
segments: These techniques engage the audience because
they create emotion and curiosity.

answer.text:
Have you ever tried to sleep while the traffic never stops outside your window? Today I will outline two ideas about noise in our city: why it is growing, and what we can do about it.

Firstly, let me explain why it is growing. Here is one statistic that surprised me: the number of cars in our city has doubled in ten years. Every new car adds more noise to our streets, and the noise does not stop at night. Moreover, the impact on our health is bigger than most people think. Noise makes us tired and nervous, and it makes it hard to concentrate at school or at work.

Secondly, what can we do? We can walk or cycle to school, we can ask the council for quiet zones, and we can talk to our neighbours about the problem. Who will make our city quieter if we do not? The council? The police? Or you and me?

To wrap up, let me recap my two ideas. The noise is growing because of traffic, and it harms our health. My takeaway is simple: small changes can make a quiet city. Thank you for listening, and I am happy to take your questions.

answer.text:
Have you ever walked past a dirty park and thought: somebody should do something? Today I will outline two ideas: the problem and a simple solution, a monthly cleaning day run by students.

Firstly, let me show you the problem. Here is one statistic that surprised me: every week, our school throws away more than two hundred kilos of paper. Last year, the park near our school was dirty for months, and nobody cleaned it. Think about the cost too: all the paper that we throw away is money that we could spend on new books.

Secondly, what can we do? I propose one Saturday a month, four groups of volunteers and two hours of work. Some people say that nobody will come, but other schools already do the same, and it works. Moreover, the impact would be bigger than the work itself: students would learn to take responsibility, and our neighbours would see that young people care. Yesterday the park was dirty; today we can make it clean. Who will do it if we do not? The council? The teachers? Or you and me?

To wrap up, let me recap my two ideas: the problem is real, and the solution is simple. My takeaway is this: a clean park begins with one Saturday. Thank you for listening, and I am happy to take your questions.
